The story of the lighthouse is not merely a tale of decay, but a meditation on the value of stillness in a world that constantly demands motion. As the tide recedes, the grey stone of the tower becomes a solid anchor in the mind. It reminds us that some things must remain fixed to provide a reference point for our own journeys.

The keeper's cottage, though cold and empty, holds a different kind of warmth. It is the warmth of memory, preserved in the fading tea tin and the deep-set windows. To look into that cottage is to look into the past. The act of remembering is an act of patience, much like the careful measurement of the coast. We often forget how much we have lost when we are so busy measuring the distance we have traveled. The spread of our measurements, rather than the average, reveals the true scale of our presence in the landscape.

As the seasons change, the lighthouse becomes a silent witness to the passage of time. The shadow it casts on the water is not a random phenomenon, but a reflection of the sun's position and the tide's movement.
